rationale: This is a mechanical rank-difference of two already-archived signals (Dual-Validated Intangible Deleveraging minus Unabsorbed External Financing), and since the unabsorbed-financing leg is by far the strongest tested effect (fmb −6.0, essentially the published external-financing anomaly), the composite will almost certainly be dominated by that leg — the very outcome the reasoning claims to avoid.

An internally consistent equal-weight rank ensemble of two previously tested legs whose evidence is complementary (one strong in Fama-MacBeth, one strong in alpha) and which deliberately excludes the dominant unabsorbed-financing channel, though it remains an ensemble rather than a new economic mechanism.

This is a cosmetic hybrid of two archive signals — Dual-Validated Intangible Deleveraging with the one-year debt change swapped for the three-year net-retirement sum used in Rent-Backed Sustained Debt Retirement — so it tests no genuinely new conditioning information.

A coherent, sign-consistent conditional amplification of the archive's best-behaved leg (Research Duration Mismatch) by a plausible refinancing-capacity proxy, with the caveat that scaling a signed variable by a low-gross-margin rank may import a gross-profitability tilt that should be checked in the diagnostics.

Both legs are, individually, well-documented negative return predictors (debt issuance/external financing and intangible-asset growth from acquisitions), so a product of two predominantly positive quantities with an EXPECTED_SIGN of positive fights the natural direction of the expression, and the specification is otherwise just the archived Contractibility-Change Financing Match with the equity leg deleted.

Sign-consistent and motivated by a real diagnosed slope/alpha divergence in the maturity-uncertainty leg, but it reuses the archive's now-standard "MIN with intangible-reinvestment gate" template, so novelty is incremental and the gate risks proxying for asset growth.
